A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaM-SLidE and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H. Added subsections and relocated figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original trajectory-prediction results for human movement, N-body systems, MD17 molecules, and tetrapeptides, plus scaling and identifier ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds an analysis of decoder attention and identifier utilization in Appendix G.6.

M1.justification: The identifier assignment, encoder-decoder architecture, latent flow model, objectives, and two-stage training remain unchanged. Appendix B.5 documents the existing procedure; the corrected main-text interpolation endpoints agree with Appendix C already present in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ETH-UCY, NBA scoring/rebounding, the three N-body scenarios, MD17, and tetrapeptides. The new attention analysis reuses MD17 Aspirin examples without extending dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and appendix comparisons, including GeoTDM's all-to-each variant and MDGen. The newly cited VN-EGNN is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: G.6 adds attention inspection using four Aspirin validation examples, models with 16 or 32 latent vectors, and shared versus distinct identifier assignments. Existing benchmark splits, prediction horizons, metrics, training budgets, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.6 examines identifier-specific attention patterns and attention-head utilization under compression. The scaling, function-evaluation, latent-count, identifier-pool, and assignment analyses in G.1–G.5 already existed in v3; their summaries in new Section 4.7 are not additional experiments.

E5.justification: The existing averaging practices and standard deviations across five random identifier assignments in Figures 7–8 are retained. The new attention visualizations add examples, without new repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–5 and 13–16 and Figures 7–8 remain unchanged. G.6 adds qualitative findings of consistent identifier attention across conformations and predominantly single-head versus two-head utilization at different latent capacities.

T1.justification: Following Eq. (6), v3 states alpha_1=sigma_0=0 and alpha_0=sigma_1=1; v4 corrects these to alpha_0=sigma_1=0 and alpha_1=sigma_0=1. This resolves an inconsistency with Appendix C. The identifier definitions, propositions, and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: fixed-size latent modeling with traceable entities, broad domain applicability, competitive performance, and favorable scalability. The new analysis supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: G.6 newly interprets stable identifier attention as a retrieval mechanism independent of stored content and suggests that using both heads under compression mitigates identifier collisions. Existing limitations and interpretations of scaling and reconstruction results are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds Python-style pseudocode for latent layers, conditioning, interpolation, loss computation, and ODE-based inference, supplementing v3's component algorithms. Existing hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Sestak et al.'s VN-EGNN as reference 86 and cites it in the introductory GNN discussion. The broader positioning relative to graph foundation models and video/language diffusion models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local grammar and phrasing edits accompany new Sections 4.7, B.5, and G.6 and the conference footer. The main organization remains intact. v4 also introduces broken appendix cross-references and corrupted spellings of scientific names in D.1.

P2.justification: v4 adds four attention figures, numbered 9–12, and formatted pseudocode. Existing reconstruction plots are relocated, and original visualization Figures 9–13 become 13–17. New Figure 12's caption states 16 latent vectors although its plotted axis indicates 32.

improvement.justification: The endpoint correction resolves v3's internal inconsistency, while B.5 and G.6 make the implementation and identifier behavior easier to assess. These provide a limited net improvement. Broken appendix references, corrupted names in D.1, and Figure 12's capacity-label mismatch detract from the presentation.
